description: Golden corpus for provisioning-event.v1; the single inventory read by the Go, Python and ajv runners (G-70). reject_by_client documents are schema-valid and refused by ParseProvisioningEvent / parse_provisioning_event on the raw token. consumer_vectors is replayed by Go and Python.

accept.why: The fullest shape: every optional envelope member present.
The minimal event: no optional members and an empty change. A user event carries no change members at all.
An email change says only that the email changed: the address is a high-cardinality identity and has no member.
Verification removed (the projected source is no longer verified). Like every user event it carries no change member.
An identity link names the principal it belongs to and the provider's short name, never the provider's subject or issuer.
A later revision of an aggregate.
Workload audiences are exact strings, bounded in count.
A grant carries its expiry (TRD section 9; Q2 default keep).
The earliest instant: year 0001 in UTC is representable in both clients.
The latest instant, six fractional digits.
Revision 2^53-1, the largest value a float64 producer represents exactly.

reject.why: No revision: nothing to deduplicate on.
No idempotency_key: the outbox column is NOT NULL and UNIQUE.
No payload.
No aggregate id.
`change` is required (it may be empty): an event that does not say what changed is not distinguishable from a malformed one.
Revisions start at 1.
Negative.
A string revision.
Exactly 2^53 as an integer token, written as RAW TEXT. A float64 producer cannot tell it from 2^53+1.
2^53+1 as an integer token, RAW TEXT (a JSON writer rounds it). Refused by the schema at its upper bound.
An aggregate type outside the closed set. Unknown denies.
aggregate_type and aggregate_id disagree in shape: an organization event carrying a prn_ id.
A grant event carrying an org_ id.
An event_type from another aggregate's vocabulary.
A verb outside the aggregate's closed vocabulary.
The key's shape is pinned: lowercase type, id, decimal revision.
An email beside the allowlisted payload members: payload is closed.
An entitlement-shaped member: entitlement is never a provisioning claim (ACP-ADR-07). A top-level member that is not an outbox column is refused.
An arbitrary key in the change object. The change is an allowlist, not a free-form map.
An email is a high-cardinality identity and has no member.
A grant member on a membership: every member exists in the schema, but each aggregate may carry only its own.
A user event carries no change members, so a credential change cannot smuggle the new hash (or anything else).
A status outside the closed vocabulary.
Repository keys are canonical lowercase owner/repo (TRD section 9).
An empty action set grants nothing; it is a malformed event, not a harmless one.
An identity event without the principal it belongs to: a consumer cannot attach the identity to anyone.
An aggregate_id of 65 characters: the idempotency_key carries at most 64.
Hour 24: Go and Python disagree about it, so the shared timestamp pattern refuses it.
request_id is fixed length and server-minted.

reject_by_client.why: Revision `1.0`: integral, schema-valid, and refused by every client on the raw token (README, wire integers).
`9007199254740990.1` reads as 9007199254740990 in a float64 reader and passes the schema; only the raw token shows it is not an integer.
`2026-02-30`: lexically valid, no such day. The pattern bounds components, not the calendar; every client refuses it.

Local fields are in range, the UTC instant is year 0000. The pattern bounds components and cannot see the composition; Python raised OverflowError on it and Go accepted it until both were pinned to one rule.
The same composition at the top: UTC year 10000.
The range rule covers the change object's timestamp too.
`2026-04-31` inside the change object: the calendar check covers every timestamp member, not only the envelope's.

idempotency_key says revision 1 while the payload says 2. Schema-valid (a pattern cannot compare members), refused by the clients: a mismatched key would let two different revisions collide in the UNIQUE index, or one revision appear twice.
idempotency_key names a different aggregate id.

consumer_vectors.description: Consumer vectors: the rule a consumer applies per (aggregate_type, aggregate_id). apply = revision is last+1 (or 1 for an aggregate never seen) and the cursor advances; ignore = revision at or below the last applied one (duplicate or stale delivery), cursor unchanged; gap = revision beyond last+1, not applied, the consumer must resynchronise, cursor unchanged. Revisions are per aggregate: interleaving aggregates never changes another aggregate's verdict. Every runner replays every case from an empty cursor.

cases.name: stale delivery after a later one
gap is not applied and does not advance
first sight above 1 is a gap
revisions are per aggregate, not global
same id in two aggregate types is two aggregates

timestamp_vectors.description: ONE timestamp rule for every timestamp member (envelope created_at, payload.change.expires_at, audit occurred_at), replayed by Go (ParseWireTimestamp) and Python (parse_rfc3339) from this list. A value is accepted when it names a real calendar day and its UTC instant lies in 0001-01-01..9999-12-31. Every vector passes the schema pattern: this is the rule the pattern cannot express.
